keeper_snapshot.definition: KEEPER. neiso-99 arm B, the JOINT arm: it settles BOTH standing NEISO owner escalations in ONE re-solve so they are not confounded (ASSESSMENT-neiso98 §4.1/§4.2). (1) AUDIT ROW O5 — the recipe moves off the ARCHIVED P2 commitment pass onto the production P1 basis; NEISO was the only keeper of six that ran, and was RENDERED FROM, P2, so every published NEISO number sat on a pass CLAUDE.md says no keeper uses. This bundle persists ['P1'] alone. (2) THE STONY BROOK ROUTING DEFECT — _resolve_unit_group's fac_group short-circuit handed a liquid-fuel combustion turbine's outage window to a sibling GAS bin, so plant 6081's two Diesel Oil CTs (83 MW each, 74 windows each) derated a 305.1 MW combined cycle they are not in for 48.7% of the 2024 and 56.0% of the 2025 capacity-year — years in which the CC units 001/002/003 have NO windows of their own at all. Three more NEISO plants were affected (1595 Kendall S6, 568 Bridgeport BHB4, 1588 Mystic MJ-1). Rule 14 [R-ACCURATE]. DETERMINATION CALIBRATED (rubric v3.3, owner amendment 2026-08-17: a ledgered C3c caveat is REPORTED at full magnitude but no longer DOWNGRADES the determination; before the amendment this run read the with-caveats determination, and no criterion moved), criterion for criterion IDENTICAL to the superseded keeper — 0 FAILs, C3c the sole ledgered caveat, C1 all 12/12 free 8/8, grade scored 8 / target 7 / commercial 0 / ledgered 1 — so NO GATE WAS TRADED for the two corrections, and rule 22 D-5(b)'s worse-determination stop does not fire. THE MOVEMENT IS DECOMPOSED, NOT CONFLATED, against the same-HEAD basis-only control 2026-08-17-neiso-99-basis-p1: the basis leg is a pure re-render (bit-identical to the incumbent's own P1, 0 differing cells every year) worth mean lambda -0.0575 / -0.0110 / -0.0378 and the 2024 annual max $256.93 -> $218.24; the routing leg is worth a further -0.0162 / -0.0133 / -0.1112 $/MWh with the annual maxima unmoved. ONE PREREG EXPECTATION IS REFUTED AND SAID SO: the routing arm's dispatch effect is dominated by KENDALL, not Stony Brook — restoring 6081's availability barely moves its dispatch because that block's heat rate 10.6062 sits above 97.5% of NEISO's CC_REGULAR capacity (cap-weighted p50 7.340), i.e. it is deep out of merit whether or not it is available, the same fact neiso-83 measured at the same plant. Frontier re-verified on THIS keeper's own sidecars (probe neiso99_declaration_recheck): C3c model tail 0 h > $300/MWh in all three years on the now-sole P1 pass, agreeing with the payload's ordc.hoursGt200.model 0/0/0 vs RT actuals 15/8/20, closest approach $280.85 (short by $19.15); the RCPF co-optimization DORMANT in all 78,840 family-hours at the published statics (1,800/1,200/600 MW) with |dual| max EXACTLY 0.0 — the prior keeper's 1.42e-14 degeneracy noise left with the P2 pass. Prereg PREREG-neiso99-p2basis-routing-2026-08-17.md, pushed before either arm solved.

keeper_snapshot.definition: NYISO KEEPER (promoted 2026-08-16, nyiso-140). Excludes the economically laid-up Port Jefferson (2517) from the always-on Long_Island ST_GAS reliability floor — a rule-17 [R-FLOOR-WINDOW] MEMBERSHIP correction, never a window change. The limb is IDENTIFIED on a fleet-aggregate when-available capacity factor but APPLIED per UNIT (pro_rata), and 2517's own CAMPD conduct is median CF EXACTLY 0.000 in every hour block of 2023/2024/2025 with 73 % of cool hours at zero, while carrying ~100 % model availability because the 2026-07-26 guard fix correctly un-booked lay-up from the outage extract. It absorbed 72.6 % of everything the limb forced (1.87 of 2.57 TWh over 3 yr) on 7.2 % of the fleet's output. The 24-hour WINDOW is confirmed CORRECT and is UNCHANGED — Barrett (2511) and Northport (2516) genuinely run the persistent cable-islanded baseline (cool-day median CF 0.254/0.313 at h00-05). floor_pct is UNCHANGED at 0.262: the two CANCELLING basis errors (a daily-mean statistic applied hourly; a fleet aggregate applied per unit) correct to 0.2666, so ZERO free parameters are added (rule 21 [R-DOF], n_residual unchanged at 6). CALIBRATED (rubric v3.3, owner amendment 2026-08-17: a ledgered C3c caveat is REPORTED at full magnitude but no longer DOWNGRADES the determination; before the amendment this run read the with-caveats determination, and no criterion moved), C3c the lone ledgered caveat — identical to the superseded keeper; C1/C2/C3a/C3b/C4/C6/C8 all PASS. A/B vs the same-HEAD control 2026-08-16-nyiso-140-control, all six pre-registered kill gates clean; K3 liveness shed 0.602/0.560/0.625 TWh against the ~0.62/yr predicted from CAMPD BEFORE any solve. DO-NOT-MISREAD: the fit gets slightly WORSE and was pre-registered to (ST_GAS err +2.679->+2.263 in 2023, -0.595->-0.916 in 2024, -3.379->-3.737 in 2025; summed |err| 6.653->6.916 TWh). It is the keeper on rule 1 [R-STRUCT] and the owner's standing structure-over-gates clause — the floor was forcing a laid-up plant, which is wrong whatever it does to the residual — and NO gated criterion regresses. Under rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] the degradation is a DISCOVERED BUG: the manufactured 1.87 TWh was masking a real downstate under-production (2025 ST_GAS already -21 % before the fix), and the successor is that root cause, never re-flooring the laid-up plant. First application of the owner-adopted K6' gate (2026-08-16): the surviving nyiso_gas_commitment_bridge share ROSE while doing strictly less work, which bare K6 would have killed. STANDING CAVEAT: K6' leg (a) leans on D-4, which is TAUTOLOGICAL for an h0-23 floor (offwindow_share 0.0 by construction), and the adopted D-4 per-unit rider is NOT yet implemented — that leg is unproven rather than passed. Evidence: results/calibration/FINDING-nyiso140-li-st-floor-membership-2026-08-16.md, PREREG-nyiso140-li-st-floor-membership-2026-08-16.md; probe scripts/probes/_nyiso140_li_st_floor_membership.py.
keeper_snapshot.label: nyiso 140 layup exclusion
